news_drafts.headline: West Sussex secures £182.7m grant to fund 90% of its schools-funding deficit to March 2026
news_drafts.lead:
West Sussex County Council has secured a High Needs Stability Grant of £182.7m, which will fund 90% of the deficit on its dedicated schools grant (the government grant that funds schools) accrued to 31 March 2026. The council's Performance and Resources Report for the second quarter of 2026/27, presented to Cabinet on 1 December 2026, says the Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Reform Plan has been approved and secures the grant. Payment is expected by the end of November 2026.

The report gives the total deficit on the grant as £204.8m after an adjustment in July. High needs is the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities. The remaining 10% of the deficit is not yet funded, and the report says national lobbying continues.

The report also records a £50m risk "linked to the Government's override ending in March 2028". The statutory override is a temporary government rule that lets councils keep a schools-funding deficit off their main balance sheet. The paper describes uncertainty over a possible 10% residual liability on the deficit, which is held off the council's balance sheet, and says the Government has not made clear what arrangements apply for 2026/27 and 2027/28.
news_drafts.paper_title: Annex B - Performance and Resources Report – Q2 2026/27

news_drafts.headline: West Sussex: government funding confirmed for 90% of schools-grant deficit, 10% still unresolved
news_drafts.lead:
West Sussex County Council says funding is confirmed for 90% of its March 2026 deficit on the dedicated schools grant, the government grant that funds schools. Its plans for reforming support for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) have been approved. The council's medium term financial strategy, before the Performance and Finance Scrutiny Committee on 30 November, says the remaining 10% and the government's arrangements for 2026/27 and 2027/28 are unresolved.

The strategy says the deficit is held off the council's balance sheet. It also says "the County Council is not in a position to absorb the residual liability, and this presents a significant risk to long term financial sustainability."

Notes of a member session on the draft 2027/28 budget say the council "has successfully met the requirements of the recovery plan process". They say the phrase "secured funding" refers to approval of the grant recovery plan. Officers acknowledged the arrangement is a reimbursement from the government and said the council would consider its wording going forward.

Appendix A of the strategy carries two separate lines for home-to-school transport for pupils with SEND, both within the children, young people and learning section. One is a projected in-year deficit of £6.0m for 2026/27. The other is annual demand growth of £4.0m for 2027/28.

news_drafts.headline: West Sussex says funding is confirmed for 90% of its schools deficit but it cannot absorb the other 10%
news_drafts.lead:
West Sussex County Council has told its Communities, Highways and Environment Scrutiny Committee that funding is confirmed for 90% of its March 2026 dedicated schools grant deficit, the government grant that funds schools, with the deficit usually arising from support for children with special needs. The council says it "is not in a position to absorb the residual liability", the remaining 10%.

The medium-term financial strategy report says plans to reform support for special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) have been approved. It says the government has not yet clarified the arrangements for 2026/27 and 2027/28. The paper describes the deficit as held off the council's balance sheet and as a significant risk to its long-term financial sustainability. The papers give no sum in pounds for the deficit or for the 10% left over.

Separately, the service pressures appendix shows SEND home to school transport with a projected in-year deficit of £6m for 2026/27. The same appendix lists a further £4m of annual demand growth for pupils with SEND on that service.

findings.paper_title: Annex B - Performance and Resources Report – Q2 2026/27
findings.headline: 2026/27 capital year-end forecast of £132.090m against £142.323m approved in February 2026
findings.detail: The revised starting budget after profile movements was £128.116m. Profiled spend has since risen by £3.974m. The paper says in-year variations are expected given the nature of capital expenditure.
findings.matters: Movement from an approved £142.323m to a £132.090m forecast shows how much of the capital programme is slipping into later years, which affects borrowing need and treasury planning.
findings.figures: £142.323m approved capital programme; £128.116m revised starting budget; £3.974m increase in profiled spend; £132.090m year-end forecast
findings.quote: Profiled spend has since risen by £3.974m, increasing the year end forecast to £132.090m.

findings.paper_title: Annex B - Performance and Resources Report – Q2 2026/27
findings.headline: Midhurst Rother College defects capital project rated Red for time and quality, Amber for cost, at £0.500m
findings.detail: The paper says meetings are ongoing between the County Council, the college and the contractor, with legal support in place. This is the only capital project listed with a Red status this quarter.
findings.matters: A defects dispute on a school building that is red on time and quality, with legal involvement, is a live contractual exposure that other councils with similar school contracts would watch.
findings.figures: £0.500m project value; Red for time, Red for quality, Amber for cost
findings.quote: Meetings are ongoing between the County Council, the college and the contractor, with legal support in place.

findings.paper_title: Annex B - Performance and Resources Report – Q2 2026/27
findings.headline: ELT estimates financial control measures could generate savings of approximately £4m in 2026/27
findings.detail: The measures include enhanced workforce controls, tighter application of service policies, maximising grant funding and reducing third-party expenditure. The paper says full financial impact is still being quantified and that benefits will appear in service budgets as realised.
findings.matters: A quantified target for in-year financial controls, set against a £34.3m overspend, shows the scale of mitigation the council expects, which peers and lenders can test against outturn.
findings.figures: approximately £4m estimated savings in 2026/27; £34.3m forecast overspend
findings.quote: it is estimated that they could generate savings of approximately £4m during 2026/27

findings.paper_title: Annex B - Performance and Resources Report – Q2 2026/27
findings.headline: Uncommitted Contingency Budget of £8.844m after £1.156m allocated to fund pay awards above 3.0%
findings.detail: The Contingency Budget started the year at £10.0m. The paper says pay awards of NJC 3.3%, Soulbury 3.6% and Fire and Rescue 3.8% against a 3.0% budget assumption required £1.156m to be allocated to portfolios. The remaining £8.844m has been excluded from the forecast.
findings.matters: The size of an uncommitted contingency held outside the forecast shows how much headroom remains against the reported overspend, and pay awards above budget are a common pressure across councils.
findings.figures: £10.0m opening Contingency Budget; £1.156m allocated; £8.844m uncommitted; NJC 3.3%, Soulbury 3.6%, Fire and Rescue 3.8% against 3.0% budget assumption
findings.quote: the remaining uncommitted Contingency Budget is £8.844m

findings.paper_title: Annex B - Performance and Resources Report – Q2 2026/27
findings.headline: Doubtful Debt Provision at £17.7m, with a possible further £6.0m requirement in 2026/27
findings.detail: The paper says the provision is being reviewed and will be finalised later in the year. Debt recovery work is underway, including additional internal and external resources.
findings.matters: A possible year-end top-up of this size would hit the revenue position and signals the council's exposure on ageing debt.
findings.figures: £17.7m Doubtful Debt Provision at 31 March 2026; around £6.0m potential additional requirement in 2026/27
findings.quote: potentially resulting in an additional funding requirement of around £6.0m in 2026/27.
